name: KY-021 mini magnetic reed switch module
description: Magnet detector: a normally-open glass reed switch between S and GND with a 10 kOhm pull-up resistor from S to the + pin. S is HIGH with no magnet and goes LOW while a magnet (about 10-20 mm away, depending on its strength) closes the reed contacts (active low). It only reports on/off, not field strength. Runs on 3.3-5 V. Sold as: Keyes / Joy-IT KY-021 mini reed magnet module (black 3-pin sensor-kit board with glass reed switch, also sold as HW-497; header S, + (middle), -).
eli5: Two tiny metal strips inside a glass tube touch when a magnet comes close, so your board can tell a door or lid has shut.

pins.name: S
pins.description: Signal (pin 1): HIGH with no magnet, LOW while a magnet closes the reed switch. Pulled up to + by the on-board 10 kOhm resistor.
Middle pin: supply for the pull-up, 3.3-5 V. Use 3V3 with an ESP32 or Pico, because S is pulled up to this voltage.

supplierQuery: KY-021 mini reed switch magnetic module
buildNotes: On an ESP32 or Pico connect + to 3V3: the on-board 10 kOhm pull-up takes S to the + voltage, so 5 V on + puts 5 V on the GPIO.
S is active LOW: 1 with no magnet, 0 while a magnet closes the reed switch.
The reeds bounce briefly when they make or break; debounce for about 20 ms (the driver's magnet() does this).
The glass reed is fragile: do not bend its leads close to the glass.
If S never changes, check that S and - are not swapped and bring the magnet alongside the glass tube.

driver.code:
# KY-021 mini magnetic reed switch module, MicroPython driver.
# The module is a normally-open glass reed switch between S and GND (-) plus a
# 10 kOhm pull-up resistor (marked 103) from S to the middle + pin. So S is:
#   HIGH (1) with no magnet nearby (reeds apart, switch open)
#   LOW  (0) while a magnet pulls the reeds together (switch closed) -> "magnet"
# The reeds bounce for a few milliseconds when they make or break, so readings
# are debounced. Power + from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V board: the pull-up takes S up to
# the + supply.
from machine import Pin
import time


class KY021:
    def __init__(self, pin, debounce_ms=20):
        # The board has its own 10k pull-up; an internal pull-up is harmless and
        # keeps the input defined if + is left unconnected.
        self.pin = Pin(pin, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP) if isinstance(pin, int) else pin
        self.debounce_ms = debounce_ms

    def raw(self):
        """Logic level on S right now: 0 = reed closed (magnet), 1 = open."""
        return self.pin.value()

    def closed(self):
        """True while the reed contacts are closed (S pulled LOW)."""
        return self.pin.value() == 0

    def magnet(self):
        """Debounced: True if S stays LOW (magnet present) for debounce_ms."""
        state = self.pin.value()
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) < self.debounce_ms:
            v = self.pin.value()
            if v != state:
                state = v
                t0 = time.ticks_ms()
            time.sleep_ms(2)
        return state == 0

    def irq(self, handler, on_close=True):
        """Call handler(pin) when the reed closes (falling edge, magnet arrives) or
        opens (rising edge, magnet leaves). Expect extra calls from contact bounce."""
        self.pin.irq(handler=handler, trigger=Pin.IRQ_FALLING if on_close else Pin.IRQ_RISING)

example.code:
from ky021 import KY021
import time

reed = KY021({S})
while True:
    print('Magnet: %s' % ('YES' if reed.magnet() else 'no'))
    time.sleep(0.5)
